prefight.pyroNova2: Every single day you ask. I'm okay, Pyro.
prefight.pyroNova3: Good. Then I'm not going easy on you.
prefight.novaRift2: Who else? Here, a star. You look like you need one.
prefight.novaRift3: Thanks. Let's fight like old times.
prefight.pyroRift1: Pyro! First one to land a hit wins.
prefight.pastFallen2: It's what you become. The Axiom showed me everything.
prefight.pastFallen3: Then I'll fight it out of both of us.
prefight.novaFallen1: Rift, it's me. Please come home.
prefight.novaFallen2: Nova. The Rift you knew is gone.
prefight.novaFallen3: Then I'll bring him back myself.
prefight.pyroFallen1: I've looked after Nova every day since you left.
prefight.pyroFallen2: Then you wasted every one of them.
prefight.pyroFallen3: Not a single one. Let's go.
prefight.novaAxiom2: I took nothing. He chose to see.
prefight.axiomPast1: There you are. Before I found you.
prefight.axiomPast2: So it's you. Not this time.
prefight.mirrorReply: Funny. I was about to say that.
prefight.pyroOpen: Hope you brought a fire extinguisher.
prefight.cryoOpen: Stay cool. This won't take long.
prefight.aeroOpen: Catch me if you can. You can't.
prefight.hydroOpen: Ride the wave or get swept away.
prefight.vitaOpen: Don't worry, I'll patch you up after.
prefight.toxiOpen: Go on, take a deep breath.
prefight.toxiReply: That's a little toxic of you.
prefight.chronoOpen: I've already seen how this ends.
prefight.shiftOpen: Which one of me will you hit?
prefight.novaReply: Cute. The stars are on my side.
prefight.spatioOpen: Space bends where I tell it to.
prefight.hexizonOpen: Player two has entered the game.
prefight.crysOpen: Hit me. I'll only shine brighter.
prefight.sandOpen: Every grain out here is mine.
prefight.sandReply: Sand gets everywhere. So do I.
prefight.pastriftOpen: Reality is more of a suggestion.
prefight.pastriftReply: Ha! Let's bend the rules a bit.
prefight.floraOpen: Careful. Everything I cut grows back.
prefight.chaosOpen: Try to keep up. Nobody does.
prefight.chaosReply: Was that it? I barely moved.
prefight.smokeOpen: Blink and you'll miss me. You'll blink.
prefight.smokeReply: Funny. I was about to say the same thing.
prefight.auroraOpen: Look up. That's the last light you'll see tonight.
prefight.glassOpen: Go on, hit me. You'll only be hitting yourself.
prefight.glassReply: Funny. You look worse from this side.
prefight.threadOpen: Every fight's a pattern. Yours ends here.
prefight.threadReply: Hold still while I stitch you up.
prefight.swarmOpen: You hear that buzzing? That's all of us.
prefight.swarmReply: One of you. Thousands of us.
prefight.rustOpen: Everything breaks down in the end. I just speed it up.
prefight.magmawOpen: I'll melt you down to slag.
prefight.riftmakerOpen: I got bored. You're my new game.
prefight.hollowOpen: Your soul looks heavy. Let me take it.
prefight.axiomOpen: The universe is tidier without you.
prefight.axiomReply: You are a mistake. I correct mistakes.
prefight.mnemovoreOpen: I'll forget you. Then you'll forget you.
prefight.elderdarkOpen: I was here before the first star.
prefight.elderdarkReply: And I'll be here after the last.
prefight.perihelionOpen: Out of my orbit, small thing.
prefight.carinaOpen: Be born again in my nebula.
prefight.velaOpen: Feel that pulse? It's counting down.
prefight.aeonOpen: I am the first light. You're a flicker.
prefight.carnaelOpen: Hold still. Reaping is quicker that way.
prefight.carnaelZenith1: Your seal broke, Zenith. Now I reap the sky itself.
prefight.carnaelZenith2: I locked you beneath the stair once. I will break every limit to do it again.
prefight.carnaelZenith3: Then let us shatter reality together!
prefight.pyroCryo1: Hope you brought a coat — wait, no, you're gonna melt!
prefight.pyroCryo2: Talk is cheap, Pyro. Let's see your flame survive absolute zero.
prefight.umbraLux1: Every light casts a shadow, Lux. Yours is mine.
prefight.umbraLux2: Only until the dawn burns it away.
prefight.electroAero1: Try keeping up with a lightning bolt!
prefight.electroAero2: You're fast, Electro, but the wind is already everywhere.
prefight.chronoGravity1: I've already seen how this ends.
prefight.chronoGravity2: Even time bends when the gravity is heavy enough.
prefight.hollowCarnael1: You copy my scythe, red one. Mine was first.
prefight.hollowCarnael2: You reap scraps of souls. I harvest the light of gods.
prefight.aeonZenith1: Let us see if the highest light still remembers the first sky.
prefight.aeonZenith2: Come, Aeon. Show me if I have grown soft.
prefight.vinculumCarnael1: Prisoner. Return to your cell. That is the sentence.
prefight.vinculumCarnael2: You opened the door yourself, Warden. No lock holds me now.
prefight.vinculumOpen: Hold out your wrists. This won't take long.
prefight.vinculumReply: Every cell has a door. Yours just closed.
prefight.obolusOpen: Your account is overdue. Seven days, with interest.
prefight.obolusReply: Everything has a price. Let's find out yours.
prefight.campanelOpen: You hear that? Nothing. That is the sound of your morning.
prefight.campanelReply: Every hour ends. Let me ring yours.
prefight.igniferOpen: You've left a lamp out. Let me fix that.
prefight.igniferReply: Hold still. This will only take a match.
prefight.orogenOpen: Hold still. I'm about to move the ground.
prefight.orogenReply: I was here before the hills.
prefight.gnarlrootReply: Then I'll pull you up by the roots.
prefight.ambrelOpen: Hold still. You'll look lovely in gold.
prefight.ambrelReply: Hush now. Stay like that for ever.
prefight.coilvastOpen: Feel the floor tilt? That's me, waking up.
prefight.coilvastReply: Come closer. I only squeeze a little.
prefight.anvilheartOpen: Hold still. I'm measuring you for the fire.
prefight.anvilheartReply: Bad work goes back in the forge. You're bad work.
prefight.primevaOpen: Hush. Listen to my heart. It's the last thing you'll hear.
prefight.primevaReply: My children are tired. You won't tire them any more.
prefight.zenithOpen: You called me down from the top of the sky. Make it worth the trip.
prefight.zenithReply: Nothing stands higher than I do.
prefight.ownOpen: I made myself for this fight.
prefight.mercOpen: Hit me as hard as you like. I just pour back.
prefight.mercReply: Good. I was getting bored of holding one shape.
prefight.alchOpen: Everything can be turned into something better. Even you.
prefight.alchReply: Lead or gold. You choose how this ends.
prefight.nadirOpen: I don't know what I can do yet. Let's find out together.
prefight.nadirReply: Whatever you hit me with, I might give back.
prefight.nadirZenith2: You climbed all this way to ask me something.
prefight.nadirZenith4: Beat me, and I might tell you.

ch5.title: Chapter 5: The Heart of the Rift

intro.l1: A crack opened in the sky above the arena last night. Nobody saw what came out of it.
intro.l2: By morning, shadows were walking on their own. They call themselves Voidlings, and they answer to one name: Nullshade.
intro.l3: Nullshade erases whatever it touches. If the rift stays open, there will be nothing left to fight for.

s1.l1: Training is over. The Voidlings are here to stay.
s1.l2: Then you can stay down. Let's go.

s2.l1: Every clock in this tower stopped when the rift opened. Yours stops next.
s2.l2: Funny. We were about to say the same thing.

s3.l1: Which one of you is real? It doesn't matter. Both of you vanish.
s3.l2: Break the mirrors, then break the acolyte.

s4.l1: Up here, one push and you're gone.
s4.l2: Good thing there are two of us.

s5.l1: Nullshade turns everything into scrap. You're next on the pile.
s5.l2: Not today. Not us.

s6.l1: The ice is thin. Fight carefully. Or don't.
s6.l2: Stay on your feet and hit hard.

s7.l1: These ruins were a city once. Nullshade was hungry.
s7.l2: Then we end this before it eats another one.

s8.l1: The storm is ours now. So is the quarry.
s8.l2: Clear them out. The Rift Gate is right behind them.

s9.l1: I am the Herald. Past this gate, there is only Nullshade.
s9.l2: Then step aside, or get moved.

s10.l1: You came all this way to be erased.
s10.l2: We came to close your rift.
s10.l3: Matter meets antimatter. Only one of us is left standing.

outro.l1: Impossible. You should have cancelled out.
outro.l2: Turns out two is more than nothing.
outro.l3: The rift shrinks to a thin line of light. Out past the coast, a storm is already gathering over the sea.

intro.l1: The last of the rift's light fell into the sea, and the sea woke up angry.
intro.l2: Ships stopped coming home. The lighthouse went dark. Past the breakwater, a whirlpool has been turning for nine days without stopping.
intro.l3: Its name is Maelstrom, and every wave on this coast answers to it now.

s1.l1: The tide pools belong to the Brine Imps now. Splash off.
s1.l2: Small fish first. Then the big one.

s2.l1: I put the lighthouse out myself. Ships crash better in the dark.
s2.l2: Then let's light the place up.

s3.l1: This ship sank in one wave. Want to see how?
s3.l2: We'd rather see you sink.

s4.l1: One slip on the cliff and the sea takes you. Maelstrom always wins.
s4.l2: Not if we never slip.

s5.l1: The caves echo. Every scream comes back twice as loud.
s5.l2: Then they'll hear yours twice.

s6.l1: You can't hit what you can't see.
s6.l2: Stay close. Swing at the thunder.

s7.l1: The market's closed. Storm tax, paid in full.
s7.l2: We're paying you back, with interest.

s8.l1: Past this wall is open water. Nobody swims home from the whirlpool.
s8.l2: We're not swimming. We're winning.

s9.l1: Captain of the tide, at your service. The eye of the storm is the calmest place to lose.
s9.l2: Calm is good. We'll hear you fall.

s10.l1: I am the sea that does not stop. Every storm you have seen was only me breathing.
s10.l3: Come into the whirlpool. Everyone does, eventually.

outro.l1: The tide is turning away from me.
outro.l2: That's what tides do.
outro.l3: The whirlpool slows, then stills. The lighthouse flickers back on, and its beam points inland, toward a column of black smoke rising over the wastes.

intro.l1: Inland, the ground is cracking open. Rivers of lava are carving new roads through the desert.
intro.l2: Something under the wastes is walking. With every step it takes, a mountain splits.
intro.l3: The Cinder Imps call it Magmaw. They say it will swallow the world one bite at a time.

s1.l1: The ash road only goes one way: down into the furnace.
s1.l2: Then we'll take it, and you're coming with us.

s2.l1: Magmaw melted this sand into glass. You're next.
s2.l2: Glass breaks. So will you.

s3.l1: The ground here eats people. I just help.
s3.l2: Watch your footing and keep moving.

s4.l1: Every bone in this canyon belonged to someone brave.
s4.l2: We're not here to add to the pile.

s5.l1: The water isn't real. Neither are your chances.
s5.l2: We'll check that for ourselves.

s6.l1: Inside the tubes, the walls never cool down.
s6.l2: Then let's make this quick.

s7.l1: This orchard burned in a minute. I'll take longer with you.
s7.l2: You won't get the chance.

s8.l1: Every step up these stairs is sharper than the last.
s8.l2: Good. We like a climb.

s9.l1: I keep the rim. Nobody looks into the caldera and walks away.
s9.l2: We're not looking. We're going in.

s10.l1: Little sparks. I have eaten mountains bigger than you.
s10.l2: Then you've never tasted anything like us.
s10.l3: The furnace is hungry. Feed it.

outro.l1: My fire is going out.
outro.l2: Rest, Magmaw. The ground needs to cool.
outro.l3: The lava hardens into black glass. Far to the north, every clock in the world stops at the same second.

intro.l1: Snow is falling in the north, and it isn't moving. Each flake hangs in the air where it stopped.
intro.l2: Time is freezing over. Birds hang mid-flight. Rivers stand still in their beds.
intro.l3: At the centre of it all is Everwinter, the winter that stopped the clocks, and it does not want them to start again.

s1.l1: Out here, nothing moves unless Everwinter allows it.
s1.l2: We're moving. Try and stop us.

s2.l1: Every book in this library ends on the same page. So does your story.
s2.l2: We'll write a new one.

s3.l1: The gears have stopped. I can see your future, and it's frozen too.
s3.l2: Then you didn't look closely.

s4.l1: The bridge holds one at a time. I'm heavier.
s4.l2: Then we'll knock you off it.

s5.l1: Quiet. The chapel has not heard a sound in a hundred years.
s5.l2: It's about to.

s6.l1: The vault keeps every lost second. You'll stay in here with them.
s6.l2: We're on a schedule.

s7.l1: The lights in the sky froze too. Beautiful, isn't it?
s7.l2: They'll look better moving.

s8.l1: The throne waits for its ruler. You will kneel in front of it.
s8.l2: We don't kneel.

s9.l1: This is the stopped hour. Nothing that enters it ever leaves.

s10.l1: Why fight? In my winter, nothing ever ends. Nothing ever hurts.

outro.l1: The ice is ticking.
outro.l2: Time's up, Everwinter.
outro.l3: The snowflakes finally fall. In the thaw, something strange shows in the meltwater: the reflection of a sky that isn't this one.

intro.l1: The rift Nullshade came through never really closed. Someone has been holding it open from the other side.
intro.l2: Through the crack lies a world of floating stone and folded space, where up and down take turns.
intro.l3: Its maker rewrites reality on a whim. The Riftmaker has been watching every fight you've won.

s1.l1: Step over the edge. The fall is the fun part.
s1.l2: We'll take the fight right here.

s2.l1: In the void, you fight your own reflection.
s2.l2: Then we already know all your moves.

s3.l1: Down is wherever I say it is.
s3.l2: Plant your feet and hit it anyway.

s4.l1: The sky broke the last time the Riftmaker got bored.
s4.l2: Let's not give it another reason.

s5.l1: Every flower here is poison. So am I.
s5.l2: Keep your distance and keep swinging.

s6.l1: Round and round. You'll forget why you came.
s6.l2: We came to win. Easy to remember.

s7.l1: Fire, water, earth and air. The court plays them all against you.
s7.l2: We brought our own.

s8.l1: Every word you say comes back twice.
s8.l2: Then listen closely. We win. We win.

s9.l1: One gate left. I fold space, and you fold in half.

s10.l1: Welcome to the core. Shall we fight on the Moon? In a nebula? I can make anywhere the arena.
s10.l2: Pick anywhere you like. We'll still beat you there.
s10.l3: Then let's see how you fall without gravity.

outro.l1: Reality is refusing to bend.
outro.l2: Some things stay put.
outro.l3: The floating stones settle. Through the last crack in the rift, a cold bell rings from a kingdom where nobody has lived for a very long time.

intro.l1: A kingdom that died long ago has started to stir. Its bells ring at midnight with no one to pull the ropes.
intro.l2: Lanterns float over the marsh. Armour walks the roads with nobody inside it.
intro.l3: On a throne of ash sits the Hollow King, gathering an army that can't be killed, because it was never alive.

s1.l1: The road is paved with old knights. Lie down and join them.
s1.l2: We'll walk over them instead.

s2.l1: Follow the lanterns. They always lead somewhere worse.
s2.l2: We'll follow them straight to the King.

s3.l1: The crypt is locked from the inside.
s3.l2: Then we'll knock.

s4.l1: The river under this bridge is made of tears. Add yours.
s4.l2: Not a chance.

s5.l1: Every skull in the ossuary was a hero once.
s5.l2: And none of them gave up. Neither do we.

s6.l1: Everything here is for sale. Souls go for two coins each.
s6.l2: Ours aren't for sale.

s7.l1: Every chain in this hall holds someone who said no to the King.
s7.l2: Then let's break a few.

s8.l1: The cathedral burned a thousand years ago. It's still warm.
s8.l2: Stay sharp. We're close.

s9.l1: I have kept vigil at the King's door since before your world began.

s10.l1: Kneel. Everyone kneels, in the end.
s10.l2: Your kingdom is empty. There's nobody left to kneel to you.
s10.l3: Then you will be my first new subjects.

outro.l1: My crown is so heavy.
outro.l2: Put it down. Rest.
outro.l3: The bells fall silent. The sky over the kingdom brightens for a moment, then goes strangely dim. Far above, the sun is starting to go out.

intro.l1: The days are getting shorter, and not because of the season. The sun is burning black from the inside.
intro.l2: Every hour, the sky gets a little darker. Shadows stretch longer than the things that cast them.
intro.l3: Something has made its home in the heart of the sun. It calls itself the Black Sun, and it is eating the light.

s1.l1: It's always dusk now. Soon it will always be night.
s1.l2: Not if we have anything to say about it.

s2.l1: The sundial has no shadow left to tell the time with.
s2.l2: We'll give it a long one. Yours.

s3.l1: This forge made the sun's crown. It'll make your grave too.
s3.l2: Hit hard, hit fast.

s4.l1: Every step closer to the sun, the hotter it gets.
s4.l2: We can take the heat.

s5.l1: The trees here grow toward the dark.
s5.l2: Then let's bring a little light.

s6.l1: The astronomers saw the Black Sun coming. Nobody believed them.
s6.l2: We believe them. That's why we're here.

s7.l1: The halo is the last ring of light. I'll snuff it out with you.
s7.l2: Two of us, one of you. Do the maths.

s8.l1: Past this gate, the sun is black all the way down.
s8.l2: Then we'll bring our own light.

s9.l1: I am the last paladin of the dusk. When I fall, nothing stands between you and the crown.

s10.l1: Look up. Every star you have ever seen, I will swallow.
s10.l2: Then you'll have to start with us.

outro.l1: The light is coming back.
outro.l2: It never really left.
outro.l3: Gold floods the sky again. When night finally falls, there is one star too many, and it is falling toward the edge of the world.

intro.l1: Every enemy you have beaten came through a crack in reality. Every crack leads back to one place.
intro.l2: Past the last star, at the edge of everything, the cosmos has woken up and given itself a will.
intro.l3: It calls itself the Axiom. It folds galaxies in its fists, and it has decided the universe would be tidier without you.

s1.l1: The stars led you here. They were never guiding you. They were herding you.
s1.l2: Then we'll follow them all the way to the end.

s2.l1: Each step up is one more proof that you can't win.
s2.l2: We've heard that seven times already.

s3.l1: In the slow orbit, every punch takes a year to land.
s3.l2: Then let's start swinging now.

s4.l1: Two stars, two of you. One of each pair burns out.
s4.l2: Not this pair.

s5.l1: The nebula shows you what you'll become: dust.
s5.l2: Dust that hits back.

s6.l1: A billion rocks, and every one of them is aimed at you.
s6.l2: Dodge left, hit right.

s7.l1: This comet stopped in its tracks the day the Axiom woke up.
s7.l2: We'll get it moving again.

s8.l1: Past the horizon, not even light comes back. You won't either.
s8.l2: We always come back.

s9.l1: I am the paradox that guards the end. You can't beat me, because you have already lost.

s10.l1: Everything you fought was a rough draft. I am the final version.
s10.l2: Then we're the edit you didn't see coming.
s10.l3: Reality ends here. Let me show you how.

outro.l1: Impossible. That outcome was not in the equations.
outro.l2: We were never good at following rules.
outro.l3: The edge of everything holds. The rift is gone for good, and every fighter who came this far has a story worth telling.

intro.l1: The Reign 8 are gone. For a while the sky stayed quiet, and the fighters went home.
intro.l2: But the cracks they tore in reality never fully closed, and something older than the stars has been listening at them.
intro.l3: Now lights rise out of the sea at night. The first herald of the Elder Dark has come to fish.

s1.l1: The water is warm tonight. Something big is turning over down there.
s1.l2: Then it can stay down there.

s2.l1: Can you hear it? Under the waves, it is singing your names.
s2.l2: It can sing all it likes.

s3.l1: Every street in this town runs downhill to the sea. You'll see why.
s3.l2: We'll take the long way back up.

s4.l1: The bell in this chapel rang for the drowned. Today it rings for you.
s4.l2: Then we'll ring it louder.

s5.l1: The tide bell rang thirteen times. The sea only counts that high for a herald.
s5.l2: Let it count. We'll still be standing.

s6.l1: Each step down this stair takes you closer to the light that eats.
s6.l2: We stopped being scared of the dark eight bosses ago.

s7.l1: Pray here, little heroes. Everyone does, near the end.
s7.l2: We'd rather fight.

s8.l1: I light the way down. Follow my lamp and you will never be cold again.
s8.l2: We're putting the lamp out.

s9.l1: You beat eight tyrants and thought the story was over. They were only loud. We are old.
s9.l3: Look at my light. Keep looking. You'll want to come closer.

outro.l1: My light goes out, but the dark behind it is wide awake. It saw you.
outro.l2: Good. Let it come up and take a proper look.
outro.l3: The sea goes still. Far above, a second crack opens in the sky, and through it something enormous turns one eye toward the world.

intro.l1: The eye in the sky looked down once, and where its gaze fell, the Mirewood began to sing.
intro.l2: Travellers who went in to listen never came out. Now the trees are wearing their voices.
intro.l3: Deep in the wood, the second herald of the Elder Dark has planted a garden. Everything in it belongs to one mind.

s1.l1: Hush. Hear it? The whole wood is humming the same note.
s1.l2: We hear it. We just don't feel like humming.

s2.l1: Stay a while. Breathe deep. The spores are kind.
s2.l2: We'll hold our breath, thanks.

s3.l1: I came here looking for my brother. Now I sing with him.
s3.l2: Then we'll get you both out.

s4.l1: This oak stood a thousand years. The rot took it in one night.
s4.l2: And we'll take it back in one fight.

s5.l1: Every one of us is a mouth. All of us are one voice.
s5.l2: Lucky for you, we're used to fighting crowds.

s6.l1: The song gets louder the further in you walk.
s6.l2: Good. We'll know we're getting close.

s7.l1: Lie down in the moss. Let it grow over you. It stops hurting after a while.
s7.l2: We'll stay standing.

s8.l1: Weeds. You are weeds in Mother's garden. I am here to pull you out.
s8.l2: Bring your shears. You'll need them.

s9.l1: Little voices. Each of you sings alone. How lonely that must be.
s9.l2: We're not alone. We're just not yours.
s9.l3: Everyone joins the choir in the end. Let me show you the harmony.

outro.l1: The song does not end. It only moves to a new garden. And the one who eats memories is already feeding.
outro.l2: Then we'll find it before it gets full.
outro.l3: The wood falls quiet and the travellers wake up in the moss, coughing. But far away, a whole city has started to forget its own name.

intro.l1: Greyhaven was the city that stood longest against the Reign 8. Its people swore they would never forget.
intro.l2: Now they can't remember the war, or their neighbours, or the way home. Streets are fading off the map one by one.
intro.l3: The third herald of the Elder Dark is eating the city's memories, and every one it swallows makes it stronger.

s1.l1: Have we met? You have the kind of face people forget.
s1.l2: We'll make sure you remember this one.

s2.l1: I filed this street under Never Was. It has stopped being there.
s2.l2: We're walking on it right now.

s3.l1: I guarded this square for a hero. I can't remember which one.
s3.l2: Then let's make some new memories.

s4.l1: I borrowed this face from a baker. He won't be needing it.
s4.l2: Give it back when we're done.

s5.l1: The records say you won a great war. Shall I tear out the page?
s5.l2: Tear all you like. We were there.

s6.l1: Every clock in Greyhaven stopped at the same minute. It forgot the next one.
s6.l2: Then we'll wind it back up.

s7.l1: Your friends, your homes, your names. Tell me the one you'd miss least.
s7.l2: None of them are on the menu.

s8.l1: I play the lives the master leaves behind. Tonight I'll play yours.
s8.l2: Sorry. We're not finished with them.

s9.l1: I know you. You beat eight tyrants and one herald of the deep. I can taste it on you.
s9.l2: Then you know how this ends.
s9.l3: Endings are only memories too. And I am so very hungry.

outro.l1: Before you came I ate the oldest memory in this city. It was of the Elder Dark, before the stars were lit. It remembers the way home.
outro.l2: Then it can forget it.
outro.l3: Greyhaven's streets come back one by one, and its people remember their names. That night the moon rises with a shadow across it, and the shadow has wings.

intro.l1: Above the Starward Peaks, the old observatory has watched the moon for three hundred years.
intro.l2: Last night its keepers watched a shape cross the moon, and then another, and then a thousand more. The moon is going dark.
intro.l3: The fourth herald of the Elder Dark has come to eat the last light in the night sky, and the brightest things on the mountain are its first meal.

s1.l1: Bright. You're so bright. Hold still.
s1.l2: You'll find we're hard to catch.

s2.l1: I swallowed a lamp once. Then another. I can't stop.
s2.l2: We'll help you stop.

s3.l1: The moon tastes of frost and silver. Soon there'll be none left.
s3.l2: Leave the moon alone.

s4.l1: I never finished hatching. The Mother says I don't need to.
s4.l2: Then you won't be needing these wings either.

s5.l1: Look how the stars go out. One by one, like lamps at bedtime.
s5.l2: We're not sleepy.

s6.l1: The keepers lit every lamp in the tower to call for help. We ate the lamps first.
s6.l2: Help's here anyway.

s7.l1: Can you feel the dust in your eyes? Soon you won't need them.
s7.l2: We've fought blind before.

s8.l1: I am the dark side of the moon. When the Mother is finished, I'll be the only side.
s8.l2: Not tonight.

s9.l1: Small lights. I have eaten suns smaller than you, in the dark between the stars.
s9.l2: Then you've never eaten anything that fights back.
s9.l3: Everything flickers out when my wings close. Come into the dark.

outro.l1: Too late, little lights. With the moon dark for one night, the door was open long enough.
outro.l2: Open for what?
outro.l3: The moon comes back, pale and scarred. But behind it the stars have moved, and they trace a shape that was never there before: something vast, waiting at the edge of the sky.

intro.l1: The night the moon went dark, the valley of Hollowmere went to sleep, and in the morning nobody woke up.
intro.l2: The farmers sleepwalk through their fields. The children all dream the same dream. Under the hills, something enormous is breathing in time with every one of them.
intro.l3: The fifth herald of the Elder Dark has slept beneath the valley since before the first dawn. Now it is dreaming the door open.

s1.l1: Shh. Lie down. The ground is soft and the night is long.
s1.l2: We've only just got up.

s2.l1: We all dream the same dream now. You'd like it. It's very dark and very quiet.
s2.l2: Sounds like a nightmare.

s3.l1: Hush now, little ones. I sang a whole village to sleep. Two more won't take long.
s3.l2: Save your voice.

s4.l1: Ninety-nine. A hundred. A hundred and one. I'm the one they never stopped counting.
s4.l2: Then let's count you out.

s5.l1: Mother put the kettle on a week ago. It's still on. We're all still dreaming.
s5.l2: Then it's time somebody woke you.

s6.l1: The cradle rocks, the windmills stop, and the whole valley breathes as one.
s6.l2: We're not breathing with it.

s7.l1: Every dream in the valley ends at the same black hill. You'll see it soon.
s7.l2: We'll see it on our own two feet.

s8.l1: Every lamp in Hollowmere is out. Yours are the last two still burning.
s8.l2: And they're staying lit.

s9.l1: Small waking things. You are a dream I had once, a long time ago, and did not like.
s9.l3: Then lie down beside me. When my eye opens, the whole world will sleep, and the Elder Dark will walk in through its dreams.

outro.l1: You woke me. For the first time in all the ages, I am awake, and I remember what I was dreaming of. A bell. A great bell, ringing the last hour.
outro.l2: What happens at the last hour?
outro.l3: Hollowmere wakes to a bright, cold morning, and the kettles finally boil. But far off on the sea cliffs, the bells of Carillon stop in the middle of a peal, and do not start again.

intro.l1: Carillon is a city of a thousand bells, built on the cliffs where the sea meets the sky. In a thousand years they have never all been silent at once.
intro.l2: Three days ago every bell stopped mid-swing. Then the birds went quiet, then the waves, then the people. Nobody in Carillon can make a sound.
intro.l3: The sixth herald of the Elder Dark is eating the noise of the world, so that nothing will hear its master coming.

s1.l1: Forty years I rang the hours. Now I ring the quiet. Listen. Can you hear it?
s1.l2: We can hear you fine.

s2.l1: Shh. Every word you say is one more thing for the Hush to eat.
s2.l2: Then we'll give it plenty.

s3.l1: I WAS THE VOICE OF THE GREAT BELL. NOW I AM ONLY THE WEIGHT.
s3.l2: Weight we can move.

s4.l1: Pull the rope. The bell swings. Nothing. Isn't it peaceful?
s4.l2: It's the worst sound we've ever heard.

s5.l1: EVERY TOWER IS QUIET NOW. ALL BUT THE LAST ONE.
s5.l2: Then the last one rings for us.

s6.l1: We took a vow of silence. The Hush made sure we would keep it forever.
s6.l2: Vows can be broken. So can you.

s7.l1: WHEN THE GREAT BELL CRACKS, THE LAST HOUR STRIKES. YOU WILL NOT HEAR IT.
s7.l2: We'll feel it, though.

s8.l1: I sang in the cathedral every evening. Now I only remember the shape of the song. Let me show you how it ends.
s8.l2: We'd rather hear how it starts again.

s9.l1: You are so loud. Your hearts, your breath, your footsteps. I will eat them all.
s9.l3: When the last bell is silent, nothing in this world will hear the Elder Dark arrive. Not even you.

outro.l1: Listen. Can you hear it now? The stars are singing. They are singing it home.
outro.l2: Then we'll go up there and stop the song.
outro.l3: The bells of Carillon ring all at once, so loud the sea answers. As the last peal fades, the sky over the cliffs splits open from one side to the other, and the Elder Dark looks down.

intro.l1: Before the first star was lit there was only the Dark. It was not cruel and it was not kind. It simply was, and it was everything.
intro.l2: Then the light came and pushed it out to the edge of the sky. For all the ages since, it has waited there, sending its heralds ahead to open the door.
intro.l3: Now the door is open. The ground breaks loose and rises toward the crack in the sky, and the only way to stop the Elder Dark is to go up and meet it.

s1.l1: Hungry. Hungry. You smell like light.
s1.l2: And you smell like the bottom of a well.

s2.l1: Hear the hymn of the stars that went out before your world was born. Soon we will add your sun to it.
s2.l2: Our sun isn't finished yet.

s3.l1: More of us coming. Always more. The Dark has no end.
s3.l2: Then we'll keep going until it does.

s4.l1: Everything falls toward the Dark in the end. Rocks. Worlds. You.
s4.l2: Not today.

s5.l1: Every herald you beat was only one finger of the hand. Now you stand in its palm.
s5.l2: Then let's see if it can make a fist.

s6.l1: The light was the mistake. We are only putting things back the way they were.
s6.l2: We like things the way they are.

s7.l1: I opened the first crack in your sky, long before your kind could look up. I have kept the door ever since.
s7.l2: Then it's time somebody closed it.

s8.l1: You beat the Lanternmaw, the Sporemother, the Mnemovore, the Dustmoth, the Somnarch and the Hush. But nobody beats the door.
s8.l2: Then we'll walk through it.

s9.l1: SMALL LIGHT. I WAS HERE BEFORE YOUR STARS, AND I WILL BE HERE AFTER THEM.
s9.l2: Then you'll have a long time to remember losing.
s9.l3: COME, THEN. COME INTO THE DARK BEFORE THE FIRST LIGHT, AND BE NOTHING WITH ME.

outro.l1: HOW? THE LIGHT WAS SO SMALL. HOW CAN SOMETHING SO SMALL PUSH BACK THE DARK?
outro.l2: Small lights are still lights.
outro.l3: The Elder Dark folds in on itself like a closing eye and falls back past the edge of the sky. Behind it the crack seals shut, and one by one the stars come back on.

intro.l1: Long before there was anyone to see them, the first stars were already old. They are the Celestials: the comets, the constellations, the lights that pushed the Elder Dark to the edge of the sky.
intro.l2: They have watched the world from above ever since and kept it in its place. Then something down there beat the Elder Dark on its own, and the Celestials did not like how bright the world had become.
intro.l3: Now a new star hangs over the snowfields of the far north, a little closer every night. It is not a star. It is Perihelion, the first of the Celestials, and it is coming down.

s1.l1: Bright little world. Too bright. We fell to put you out!
s1.l2: You fell. That part went fine.

s2.l1: More of us fall every night. Soon the snow will burn blue all the way to the sea.
s2.l2: Then we'd better stop the thing you're falling off.

s3.l1: Hit the ground hard. Got up harder. You next.
s3.l2: You're not the first rock we've beaten.

s4.l1: The solar wind sings to us. It sings that your world has wandered out of its place.
s4.l2: Our world is right where we left it.

s5.l1: Crater. Big. You. Small.
s5.l2: Small hits hard too.

s6.l1: Look up! It is so close now you can feel it on your face.
s6.l2: We can. And we're still not running.

s7.l1: I passed this world when it was all fire, and again when it was all ice. Each time it looked smaller than you think it is now.
s7.l2: Then this time, take a better look.

s8.l1: Little world. You pushed back the Dark by yourselves, and now you burn too brightly to be left alone.
s8.l2: So you came all this way to tell us off?
s8.l3: I came to put you back in your place. Hold still, and the fire will be quick.

outro.l1: Impossible. I have crossed this sky ten thousand times, and nothing has ever turned me around.
outro.l2: There's a first time for everything.
outro.l3: Perihelion breaks into a shower of blue sparks that drift up and up, back into the sky. Far above, between the stars, something holding a spear turns to watch.

intro.l1: The Celestials do not hunt alone. The oldest of them, Asterion, has run across the night since before the first sunrise, and every beast in the sky runs with him.
intro.l2: He saw Perihelion fall, and he saw who knocked it down. Now there is a new shape in the sky every night: a spear, pointing at the world.
intro.l3: On the high plateau of Starfall Reach the old standing stones are glowing again. That is where the Hunter will land, and that is where he expects to find his prey.

s1.l1: Grr. You smell like falling stars. The Hunter wants you.
s1.l2: He'll have to catch us first.

s2.l1: Every note I play moves a star. Listen: this one moves you.
s2.l2: Let's see how you like our music.

s3.l1: The pack found your trail. The pack always finds the trail.
s3.l2: Then the pack can follow us home, sit and stay.

s4.l1: I have carried the sky on my horns since before your mountains were born. You are not heavy.
s4.l2: We're heavier than we look.

s5.l1: The spheres are singing your last song. It is a short one.
s5.l2: We know a few more verses.

s6.l1: Once I chased the Hunter across half the sky. Now I guard his gate. That is how much he wants you.
s6.l2: Then he can come and get us himself.

s7.l1: My sting is the brightest red in the night. It will be the last light you see.
s7.l2: We've stood in the dark before the stars. Your sting doesn't scare us.

s8.l1: So this is the prey that broke a comet. Small. Fast. Brave.
s8.l2: We're not prey.
s8.l3: Everything under the sky is prey. I have hunted since before the first dawn, and I have never missed.

outro.l1: Missed. I missed. In all the ages of the sky, I have never missed.
outro.l2: Maybe you were aiming at the wrong thing.
outro.l3: Asterion's stars come loose one by one and rise back into the night, until only his belt is left: three stars in a row. Above them the sky turns, and three more Celestials begin to look down at the world.

intro.l1: Two Celestials have fallen, and the sky has started to whisper about it. Far to the south, over the white salt of the Mirror Flats, the night has turned rose and green.
intro.l2: That glow is Carina, the Star Mother: a cloud so vast that new stars are born inside her. She lit half the lights in the sky, and she thinks the world is shining where only her children should.
intro.l3: She has come down to draw her veil over it. If the cloud closes, the world goes dark underneath, and her newborn stars will be the only light left.

s1.l1: I was born last night! Mother says I'm going to be the brightest thing you ever see.
s1.l2: Born last night and already picking fights.

s2.l1: Breathe me in. Everything goes soft and pink, and then it goes away.
s2.l2: We'll hold our breath.

s3.l1: Not a star yet. Getting tighter. Getting hotter. Getting ANGRY.
s3.l2: Maybe come back when you're finished.

s4.l1: The veil is closing. Can you feel the sky getting closer?
s4.l2: We can feel you getting closer. That's worse for you.

s5.l1: Mother made a hundred of us tonight. You can't put out a hundred stars.
s5.l2: We've had a busy few books. Watch us.

s6.l1: I have stood in her cloud since before your sun was lit. Stars are born at my tips. Nothing gets past my feet.
s6.l2: Then we'll go round.

s7.l1: You broke a comet and made the Hunter miss. Mother is waiting for you. She isn't angry. That is what should scare you.
s7.l2: We've met angry. We can handle calm.

s8.l1: Look at you. So bright, and so small. I have made more stars than there are grains of salt on these flats.
s8.l2: Then you won't miss one little world keeping its own light.
s8.l3: Every light in the sky is mine. Sleep now, little ones. The veil is coming down.

outro.l1: My cloud is thinning. I can see straight through myself.
outro.l2: Turns out the world can shine without you.
outro.l3: Carina comes apart into soft colour and drifts back up into the night. Where she was, the stars she made go on burning, small and new. And far off, past the edge of the sky, something begins to tick.

intro.l1: Every star burns out in the end. Vela was the first that did, and it never stopped spinning. Its heart crushed down to the size of a city, it turns a hundred times a heartbeat and keeps the time of the whole sky.
intro.l2: Two beams of fire sweep out from it like a lighthouse. Every night they cross the deserts of the east, and wherever they touch, the sand turns to glass.
intro.l3: Vela has counted every second since the first stars were lit. Now it says the world's time is up, and it has come down to the Glasslands to stop the clock.

s1.l1: On. Off. On. Off. Which one was the real me? Too slow!
s1.l2: We'll just hit both.

s2.l1: Kssshh... can you hear it? The pulse... the pulse is counting you down... kssshh.
s2.l2: Change the station.

s3.l1: Was dune. Beam came. Now glass. Now big. Now you.
s3.l2: Glass breaks.

s4.l1: Vela spins a hundred times a heartbeat. How fast do you spin?
s4.l2: Fast enough to get out of your way.

s5.l1: Every star in the sky keeps time to Vela's beat. Soon your world's beat stops.
s5.l2: Ours has a few left in it.

s6.l1: I circled Vela when it was still a star. I burned out too, but I never left its side. Nobody stops it turning.
s6.l2: Loyal. We respect that. We still have to get past you.

s7.l1: Hear that? Tick. Tick. That's the clock you came to stop. It's very, very close now.
s7.l2: Good. We were looking for it.

s8.l1: Tick. You are late. Tick. You were always late. Tick. Your world's time ran out the night it outshone us.
s8.l2: Then we'll wind it back up.
s8.l3: I keep the time of the sky. Nobody winds me. Hold still, and I will count you out.

outro.l1: My spin... it's slowing. I can hear the seconds falling out of me.
outro.l2: Take a break. You've been going for a while.
outro.l3: Vela's beams flicker and go dim, and it settles into the glass like a stopped watch. For the first time in an age, the sky has no beat to keep. High above, the oldest of the Celestials opens its eye.

intro.l1: Four Celestials have fallen, and the sky has gone quiet. No comet, no Hunter, no glowing cloud, no beat. One light is left up there, and it is the oldest of them all.
intro.l2: Aeon was the first star that ever burned. It lit the sky, it drove the Dark out of it, and then it sat at the top of everything and watched. It has been watching ever since.
intro.l3: Now its eye has opened over Zenith, the highest mountain in the world, where the clouds lie below like a sea. Aeon has decided the world is too bright to be allowed. To stop it, your fighters will have to climb.

s1.l1: I left Aeon before your world was made. I have come SO far. Do you know how long that took?
s1.l2: Long enough to get tired, we hope.

s2.l1: I have watched this patch of sky since the beginning. Nothing new has ever come into it. Until you.
s2.l2: Then look closely. You'll want to remember this.

s3.l1: Ate... my planets. Still... hungry. You... look... small.
s3.l2: We're also very hard to chew.

s4.l1: The stars are leaning down to watch. Nothing has ever climbed this high to fight Aeon before.
s4.l2: Then let's give them a good one.

s5.l1: Comet, Hunter, Mother, Clock. We saw all of it, and so did Aeon. It was not impressed.
s5.l2: It's about to be.

s6.l1: I am the North Star. Every lost traveller who ever lived found their way home by me. You will not find your way past me.
s6.l2: We're not lost. We know exactly where we're going.

s7.l1: This is the top of the world. Above here there is only Aeon, and Aeon has never lost.
s7.l2: Everyone says that right before the last stage.

s8.l1: I lit the first light in the sky. I drove the Dark out with my own fire. Then for an age I watched you shine brighter and brighter, as if the light were yours.
s8.l2: Some of it is. We made it ourselves.
s8.l3: Nothing shines that I did not light first. I will take it back, every spark of it, and the sky will be as it was on the first night: mine.

outro.l1: So bright... You were always this bright. I never looked closely enough to see that the light was your own.
outro.l2: There's room up there for both of us.
outro.l3: Aeon's great eye slowly closes. The light it gathered streams back up into the sky, star by star, until the night is full again. On the summit of Zenith the first star rests, and for the first time in an age, it isn't keeping watch alone.

intro.l1: The Celestials are back in the sky, and for a while the world is quiet. Then, one morning, the ground starts to hum.
intro.l2: Long before the first star was lit, the world was built by the Titans: giants of stone, root and amber who raised the land and then lay down under it to sleep. When the Celestials came crashing down, the shaking woke them.
intro.l3: The first to wake is Orogen, a whole mountain range with a body. It raised the highlands, and now it has decided they are crowded. To stop it, your fighters will have to cross the hills while the hills are still moving.

s1.l1: Bounce! Bounce! The mountain's awake and so am I!
s1.l2: Great. Can you be awake somewhere else?

s2.l1: Ten thousand years in one field. Then somebody built a fence round me.
s2.l2: That was a long time ago, and it wasn't us.

s3.l1: Every stone on this hill rolled down off Orogen. We all want to go back up.
s3.l2: Then you'll have to get past us first.

s4.l1: I hear the mountain breathing. It says the land was flatter, and quieter, before you came.
s4.l2: It also says it's been asleep for a very long time.

s5.l1: I have watched every sunrise since the world was raised. I have never needed to move. Until today.
s5.l2: Then let's make it worth the trip.

s6.l1: Above me there is only Orogen, and Orogen is the ground you stand on.
s6.l2: Then we'll stand our ground.

s7.l1: I raised these hills out of the sea before the first star burned. I lay down under them so they would stay. And you built on me.
s7.l2: We didn't know you were there. Nobody did.
s7.l3: Now you do. Every road, every wall, every town: I will shrug them off, and the land will lie flat and still, the way I made it.

outro.l1: You stand on me so lightly... All this time I felt your weight, and never your steps.
outro.l2: Go back to sleep. We'll walk carefully.
outro.l3: Orogen sinks back into its range, peak by peak, until the highlands are only hills again and the jade light fades out of the cracks. But deep under the forest to the east, something with roots has felt the shaking too.

intro.l1: East of the highlands lies the Elderwood, a forest so old that its trees have trees growing on them.
intro.l2: Under it, under everything, run the roots of Gnarlroot: the first tree, the Titan that holds the world together from below. Every country in the world stands on one of its roots.
intro.l3: Gnarlroot has woken and looked up, and it does not like what is growing on its roots. It has decided the world needs weeding. To stop it, your fighters will have to go into the forest, and then under it.

s1.l1: Hush. The forest is waking up. It is waking up angry.
s1.l2: We've met a singing forest before. An angry one can't be worse.

s2.l1: Which way are you? Which way am I? Doesn't matter. Prickle!
s2.l2: Ow. Yes. Very prickly.

s3.l1: Every spring I sing the forest awake. This year Gnarlroot gave me new words.
s3.l2: Then we'll teach you an old song. It's called going home.

s4.l1: This tree fell before anyone remembers, and we grew out of it. Gnarlroot will grow out of your towns the same way.
s4.l2: Not while we're here.

s5.l1: I was Gnarlroot's first seedling. A thousand rings, and I have never let anyone down to the roots.
s5.l2: There's a first time for everything.

s6.l1: Down here there is no sun. Only roots, and the one they all belong to.
s6.l2: Then let's go and meet it.

s7.l1: Everything you stand on, I hold up. Every field, every road, every city. I held the world together while you grew on me like moss.
s7.l2: We never asked you to let go.
s7.l3: No. You never asked anything. So I will pull every weed out by the root, and the world will be a forest again, and only a forest.

outro.l1: Moss... You were never moss. You were seeds. And seeds that grow are what I was for.
outro.l2: Then keep holding on. We'll look after what's on top.
outro.l3: Gnarlroot's roots ease back into the dark, and above them the Elderwood goes still and green. But far under the roots, where the sap of the first tree pools and hardens, a light the colour of honey is beginning to glow.

intro.l1: Under the roots of the first tree, old sap has been dripping for longer than there has been time. It has pooled, and set, and become a cavern of living amber.
intro.l2: This is Ambrel, the third Titan, the world's memory. Whatever it wants to keep, it seals in gold for ever: the first leaf, the first feather, the last song of a bird no one has heard in an age.
intro.l3: Now Ambrel has woken and looked at the bright, noisy world above, and it wants to keep that too. All of it, perfect and still. To stop it, your fighters will have to go down into the gold before it sets.

s1.l1: The herd went that way. Long ago. I will find them. Out of my way.
s1.l2: They're not down here. Nobody is, except us.

s2.l1: Bzzz! I waited a hundred million years! Do you KNOW how long that is?
s2.l2: Longer than this fight is going to take.

s3.l1: Ambrel set my bones in gold so nothing could ever break them. Try.
s3.l2: We'd rather not, but all right.

s4.l1: Slower... slower... you'll like it in the web. Nothing ever changes in the web.
s4.l2: That's exactly why we won't.

s5.l1: One golden afternoon, my whole hive was sealed. I have waited ever since to finish that afternoon.
s5.l2: Then let's finish it now, and let you all go.

s6.l1: Feel the air? It is setting. In a little while you will not be able to move, and you will be beautiful for ever.
s6.l2: We'd rather keep moving.

s7.l1: I keep what matters. The first leaf. The first feather. The last song of a bird that no longer sings. Up there, everything you love fades. In here, nothing ever does.
s7.l2: Things fade. That's how we know they mattered.
s7.l3: Then let me spare you the grief. I will seal your whole bright world in gold, every face, every voice, and it will be perfect, and it will never, ever end.

outro.l1: You crack the gold so easily... Maybe a thing is not kept by holding it still. Maybe it is kept by being remembered.
outro.l2: We'll remember you. Promise.
outro.l3: Ambrel's amber softens and lets go: the leaf, the feather, the hive, the old bird's song drifting free into the dark. The hollow dims to a gentle glow. But far below it, past the last of the gold, something enormous turns over in its sleep.

intro.l1: Below the amber there is no more gold, only dark: a cavern so wide its far wall is out of sight, and a sea that has never once seen the sun.
intro.l2: This is the home of Coilvast, the fourth Titan, a serpent as long as the world. It lies coiled round the burning heart of everything, and its coils are what hold the ground together.
intro.l3: Now it has woken, and it has started to uncoil. Up above, mountains lean and rivers spill their banks. To stop it, your fighters will have to go down into the dark and wake it the rest of the way.

s1.l1: Light! Who brought light down here? Put it out. Put it out at once.
s1.l2: Sorry. We'll be quick.

s2.l1: I have seen the serpent dream. It dreams of letting go. It dreams of everything falling.
s2.l2: Then it's time somebody woke it up.

s3.l1: I live beside the coils. I eat what falls off them. Lately a great deal has been falling off them.
s3.l2: We'll try not to add to the pile.

s4.l1: Every time it turns, a city up there shakes. It is turning more and more. Can you feel it?
s4.l2: We can. That's why we're here.

s5.l1: The water down here is warm. It never used to be. The heart is close now, and so is he.
s5.l2: Good. We were getting cold.

s6.l1: I was the first scale it ever shed. I have guarded this road for the whole life of the world. You will not reach its head.
s6.l2: We just need a word with it. A short one.

s7.l1: For longer than there have been days, I have held this world together in my coils. Never once loosened. Never once slept well. I am tired, little ones.
s7.l2: Then rest. But don't let go.
s7.l3: Rest? The only rest I have ever wanted is to stretch out, all of me, just once. If the world falls apart when I do, that is the world's problem.

outro.l1: You held on... the way I always have. Perhaps I am not the only one holding things together any more.
outro.l2: You're not. Get some sleep. We'll keep watch.
outro.l3: Coilvast draws its coils tight round the heart of the world and lays its great head down, and above it the mountains settle and the rivers find their beds again. But the heat of the core is rising, and in it, something has started to burn.

intro.l1: Under the serpent's coils the dark turns red, then orange, then a white too bright to look at. This is the core of the world, and it is not a fire. It is a forge.
intro.l2: Its smith is Anvilheart, the fifth Titan, who hammered the mountains and the seas into shape when the world was new, then set down its tools and fell asleep beside them.
intro.l3: Coilvast's turning stirred the coals. The smith has woken, looked at what it made, and decided to start again. Every blow of its hammer shakes the ground above, and the next one could flatten everything.

s1.l1: Visitors! Nobody visits the forge. Nobody ever visits. Stand still so I can set you on fire.
s1.l2: We'd rather not, thanks.

s2.l1: In, out. In, out. The forge has to breathe. Stop me breathing and the fire goes out. Do you want the fire to go out?
s2.l2: Just the big one with the hammer.

s3.l1: I carry ore. The smith says more ore. Always more ore. It is making something very big.
s3.l2: That's what we're worried about.

s4.l1: Every time the hammer falls, a mountain somewhere gets a little flatter. Listen. There goes another one.
s4.l2: Then we'd better hurry.

s5.l1: Hot enough for you? It gets hotter. It always gets hotter, the closer you get to the anvil.
s5.l2: We've come this far. A bit more heat won't stop us.

s6.l1: I was the first thing it ever made. I was red-hot once, and plunged into the sea, and I came out hard. You have not been through the fire. Turn back.
s6.l2: We've been through four Titans. That's fire enough.

s7.l1: Look at it. Lumpy mountains. Crooked rivers. Seas in all the wrong places. I made the world in a hurry, little ones, and I have hated the seams ever since.
s7.l2: People live in those seams.
s7.l3: Then they go back in the fire with the rest. Every smith knows it: when the work is bad, you melt it down and start again.

outro.l1: You do not bend... you do not break... Perhaps the work was not so bad after all.
outro.l2: It's lumpy. We like it lumpy.
outro.l3: Anvilheart lays down its hammer, and the ringing in the deep slowly fades. In the quiet, your fighters hear what the forge had been drowning out all along: a heartbeat, slow and enormous, from the very middle of the world. The Titans were never the only ones down here. They were its guards.

intro.l1: Past the forge the tunnels turn warm and soft, and the walls are lined with veins of red crystal that brighten and dim in time with a heartbeat.
intro.l2: At the very middle of the world lies Primeva, the first Titan and the mother of the other five. She dreamed the world, set her children to guard her sleep, and has slept ever since, her heartbeat keeping everything alive.
intro.l3: Now she is awake, and she has found her children beaten and tired. She means to call all five of them home into her heart, and without them the world above will come apart. To stop her, your fighters will have to reach the heart of the world.

s1.l1: Ba-dum. Ba-dum. I'm a little piece of the heartbeat. Ba-dum. Do you like my rhythm?
s1.l2: It's catchy. Please move.

s2.l1: Every vein in the world runs through here, and I stitch them shut when they crack. You two I think I'll tie in a knot.
s2.l2: We've just been through five Titans. A knot won't hold us.

s3.l1: Crack me open. Go on. There's nothing inside but more crystal, and all of it is very, very hard.
s3.l2: We've cracked harder.

s4.l1: Hear how fast it beats now? She's angry. She heard what you did to her children.
s4.l2: We didn't hurt them. We asked them to stay.

s5.l1: Five gates, one for each child: stone, root, amber, coil and fire. They're all open now. Her children are coming home.
s5.l2: Not if we get there first.

s6.l1: Before the five, there was me. I kept her door when the world was only a dream. Nobody has ever walked past me.
s6.l2: Then today's a first.

s7.l1: Five children I made. Stone and root, amber and coil and fire. I gave them to the world, and the world sent you to knock them down.
s7.l2: We didn't come to hurt them. We came to ask them to stay.
s7.l3: They are tired. I can feel it in my heart. So I will call them home, every one, and the world can fall apart without them. It was only ever a dream.

outro.l1: You fight the way they do... holding on and on, for things that were never yours to hold. Is that what they learned up there?
outro.l2: No. That's what they taught us.
outro.l3: Primeva's heart slows. Far above, five great shapes stir in their places, and not one of them comes home. Stone holds, roots grip, amber glows, coils tighten and the forge burns low and steady. The mother of the Titans listens to her children choosing the world, and closes her eyes.

intro.l1: The heart of the crown is broken, and the four it held are free. For a long moment the sky is completely still. Then, far above the clouds, a stair of gold light begins to unfold, one step at a time.
intro.l2: Zenith made the stars. It hung the sun and set the sky turning, and long before any of this began, it gave a few chosen beings a share of its own power and kept them close. Nothing has ever climbed to where it sits.
intro.l3: Now it has opened the way, and it is waiting at the top. It wants to meet whoever broke its crown. To reach it, your fighters will have to climb past every one of its Chosen.

s1.l1: Wings! Look, I have wings! Zenith made them for me this morning. Watch how fast I come down!
s1.l2: Fast is fine. Landing is the hard part.

s2.l1: The hymn began when the sky was made, and I have sung it ever since. It does not stop for anyone, least of all you.
s2.l2: Then we'll fight to the beat.

s3.l1: Zenith pulled me out of a fallen star and hammered me into shape. I'm still hot. Touch me and see.
s3.l2: We'll pass on the touching, thanks.

s4.l1: This pillar holds up a corner of the sky. If I put it down, the sky falls. So I'll fight you with it on my back.
s4.l2: That sounds like a lot of pressure.

s5.l1: Zenith lent me hours from the end of the world. I can spend a few on you. You won't get them back.
s5.l2: We'll take our chances with the time we've got.

s6.l1: We fly, we sing, we sing while we fly! Isn't the stair beautiful from up here?
s6.l2: It is. We'd like to see the top.

s7.l1: Star iron and heaven's stone. You won't find anything harder anywhere in the world.
s7.l2: We've heard that before. From a Titan.

s8.l1: I knelt before Zenith, and it set a star from its own crown in my halo. I guard these stairs. No one has ever passed me, and no one ever will.
s8.l2: We just broke the rest of that crown. Let's see about yours.

s9.l1: There are so many of us now! Zenith says you're the first ones who ever got this far.
s9.l2: Then you'd better get used to us.

s10.l1: Every step from here holds up more of the sky. Can you feel it getting heavier?

s11.l1: Zenith broke this shard off the Millennium Scepter and gave it to me alone. It cuts through anything. Air. Time. You.
s11.l2: It'll have to catch us first.

s12.l1: The sun is setting on the stair. When it is gone, only the stars will see you fall.
s12.l2: Then let's give them something to watch.

s13.l1: There you are! Master told me all about you. I have been waiting at these doors since you set foot on the tenth step. Hehehe...
s13.l2: You're the one who was standing behind Zenith. We wondered when you'd show up.
s13.l3: Master wants to know what is inside you. So hold still while I open you up and have a look. HAHAHAHA!

outro.l1: Hehe... heh... You really are something. Master was right to be curious about you.
outro.l2: Go and tell Zenith we're coming.
outro.l3: Tetrael laughs one last time as its four wings fold shut around it. Then it scatters into feathers, and the feathers blow up the stair towards the throne.

s14.l1: So you are the ones who broke my crown. I made the stars you fight under. I gave my Chosen everything they have. And still you climbed.
s14.l2: We didn't come to take anything. We came to see who was up here.
s14.l3: Then look. This is the highest point there is, and no one has ever beaten me on it. Come, and I will show you everything I am.

outro.l1: ...Nobody gave you your power. You found it by yourselves, down there where I never looked. Is that how you climbed so high?
outro.l2: That, and we never stopped.
outro.l3: Zenith's hands fall open, and whatever it was holding fades into light. One by one its Chosen kneel on the stair. For the first time since it made the stars, someone other than Zenith is standing at the highest point in the sky.

vision.l1: Far above the stair, at the very top of the sky, Zenith stands at the edge of its throne with its hands folded behind its back, watching your fighters climb. In the dark behind it, something with four wings is waiting.
vision.l2: Ten steps climbed, and ten of my Chosen beaten. No one has ever come this far. I made every star in this sky, and I did not make them.
vision.l3: Here is what will happen. They will climb past the last of my Chosen, the way they climbed past all the others. Then they will reach the doors of my throne, and you will be there waiting for them.
vision.l4: I want to know what they are and where their power comes from. Break them open and show me. If they are still standing when you are done, I will come down and meet them myself.
vision.l7: Light swallows the top of the sky. When it fades, Zenith stands alone, and the dark behind its throne is empty.

intro.l1: Long before the first arena was built, Zenith ruled the ground as well as the sky, and every power under it served Zenith, even the great bosses: Nullshade, Maelstrom, Magmaw, the Hollow King and the rest of the Reign 8.
intro.l2: Then word came up out of the ash. Bosses who were tired of kneeling were gathering in secret at the foot of the stair. The Hollow King heard it first and called the Reign 8 together to put the rebellion down before it spread, and Aeon was sent up the stair to warn Zenith.
intro.l3: The first rebel fire burns in a valley of ash, and the one who lit it hangs its lantern over the black water. It is the Lanternmaw, and every boss with a grudge is following its light.

s1.l1: The light called, and we came up out of the deep. Nobody down here kneels to Zenith anymore.
s1.l2: Then you can kneel to us. Back into the water.

s2.l1: The Hollow King's hounds, sniffing round our fires. The Lanternmaw said you would come.
s2.l2: The Hollow King sends its regards. Put the fires out.

s3.l1: Every boss who ever knelt is welcome at our fires. Why are you two still on the wrong side?
s3.l2: We're on Zenith's side. That's the only side there is.

s4.l1: We are three tonight, and by morning we will be thirty. You can't put out every fire in the valley.
s4.l2: Watch us.

s5.l1: The lantern is lit, and the whole valley can see it. You're too late to stop the rebellion.
s5.l2: It's one lantern. We'll take it down ourselves.

s6.l1: Look at you, the great Reign 8, running errands for the light at the top of the stair. Come closer. Everyone comes to the lantern in the end.
s6.l2: We're not here for your light. We're here to put it out.
s6.l3: Then come and try, little loyal things. The deep is very patient.

outro.l1: The light... flickers... but it was never mine alone. Look behind you. Every fire in the valley is still burning.
outro.l2: Then we'll put them out one at a time.
outro.l3: The Lanternmaw lays its lantern down at their feet and sinks into the black water. But on the hills above the valley more banners are going up, and far above them all, Aeon is still climbing the stair with its warning.

intro.l1: The Warden's lock is broken, and the stair is cracking from the bottom up. Red light pours out of every step the rebels have climbed.
intro.l2: The rebels thought Zenith's light was only a throne. Nobody told them what it was holding down. Under the stair, under the floor of the world, something with four wings has waited a very long time for that light to go dim.
intro.l3: Its name is Carnael, and the rebels have welcomed it as their champion. With the reaper climbing behind them, their last armies push for the top of the stair.

s1.l1: We were never born under any star, and we will never kneel to one. The reaper is coming, and Zenith's sky ends tonight.
s1.l2: Not while we're standing on this stair.

s2.l1: We dreamed of this. A red sky, and no light at the top of it. Go back to sleep, loyal ones.
s2.l2: Wake up. Your dream is about to end.

s3.l1: The stone under us is bleeding red light. The rebellion is almost at the throne.
s3.l2: Almost isn't good enough.

s4.l1: Carnael reaped light before Zenith lit the first Chosen. Tonight it reaps it all, and we are the ones who let it out.
s4.l2: Then you'll be the ones who regret it.

s5.l1: This is the last step before the throne, and the reaper is right behind you. Run while you still can.
s5.l2: We didn't come this far to run.

clash.l1: The top step splits in two. Red light pours out of the crack, and Zenith comes down from its throne for the first time in an age to stand over it.
clash.l2: Zenith. You built your whole sky on top of me and called it a throne. Your own bosses opened my door. Did you think the seal would hold once your light went dim?
clash.l3: I thought I would never have to look at you again. Go back down, Carnael. I put you there once.
clash.l4: You were brighter then. Let's see how bright you are now.
clash.l5: Gold and red crash together across the top of the sky. Every blow shakes the stair to its roots, and the bosses on both sides can only watch.
clash.l6: Every star in this sky is mine. You will not reap a single one of them.
clash.l7: I don't need your stars. I only need you. Kneel. The harvest starts with you.
clash.l8: Zenith! I was sent up the stair to warn you of the rebellion. I came too late for the warning, but not for the fight.
clash.l9: Aeon... Then lend me your light, first star. One of us cannot do this alone.
clash.l10: The oldest light and the highest take each other's hands. For one heartbeat the whole sky goes white, and when it clears there is only one of them.
clash.l11: We are the first light and the last. Turn around, reaper. There is nowhere left in this sky for you to hide.
clash.l12: Two gods for the price of one. Good. The harvest was getting thin.

outro.l1: Ha... ha... Your light was always too bright to look at. I'll be back the moment it dims again...
outro.l2: Then nobody lets it dim again. Not ever.
outro.l3: Carnael breaks apart into red ash, and the crack in the stair seals itself shut. Zenaeon parts back into two lights, and the rebellion ends where it began, at the foot of the stair, with its banners on the ground. Zenith sends the rebel bosses away to the far edges of the world, and gives every boss who stood with it a corner of its own to rule. That is where, an age later, Story finds them.

intro.l1: The stair is dark, and the light at the top of the sky is still flickering. The loyal bosses hold the hundredth step and wait for word from Aeon.
intro.l2: Under the stair, in a prison cut for a single prisoner, lives its keeper: Vinculum, the Chain Warden. Its lock was only ever as strong as Zenith's light, and the rebels have promised it the one thing it has wanted for an age.
intro.l3: To be done guarding. All it has to do is open the cell. Vinculum has come up the stair with its keys, and the rebellion's armies are clearing its way down.

s1.l1: We came up out of the deep sea when the lamps went out. The Warden says something under the stair wants to meet you.
s1.l2: We're not interested. Back into the deep.

s2.l1: The amber held us for an age. The Warden is letting everyone out today. Everyone.
s2.l2: Some things stay locked up for a reason.

s3.l1: Every chain on the stair is singing the same word: open. Can you hear it?
s3.l2: We hear it. We're not listening.

s4.l1: A thousand cells under the stair, and only one was ever used. The Warden is going down to open it.
s4.l2: Then we're going down to stop it.

s5.l1: Turn back. The Warden made the lock and the key, and the key is in its hand. Whatever comes out, the rebellion wanted it.
s5.l2: Then the rebellion doesn't know what it's asking for.

s6.l1: Halt. For an age I have stood guard over one door, and no one ever asked if I wanted to. The rebels asked.
s6.l2: Do you even know what's behind that door?
s6.l3: It does not matter. Tonight it opens, and I am free. Hold out your wrists, visitors.

outro.l1: Stop... it was never meant to open. I only wanted to stop guarding it.
outro.l2: Vinculum, what's behind that door?
outro.l3: Vinculum's great padlock cracks down the middle and falls from its chest. Far below, a door that has been shut since before the first Chosen swings open, and red light comes up through the steps. Even the rebels stop climbing to stare at it.

intro.l1: The Lanternmaw's fire went out, but the rebellion did not. By the next morning, a dozen more banners were flying along the ash road.
intro.l2: Every village on that road pays Zenith in light. That week, for the first time, not one lamp's worth of it reached the stair.
intro.l3: Someone was taking the tithe before it got there: the one Zenith trusted to collect it. Obolus, the Tithe Taker, has joined the rebellion, and it is carrying Zenith's own light off to the rebels' camp.

s1.l1: Who are you? Who am I? It doesn't matter. The Mnemovore says Zenith's name is the next thing we forget.
s1.l2: Then we'll remind you.

s2.l1: The tithe carts are ours now. Every drop of light in them is going to the rebels' fires.
s2.l2: That light belongs to Zenith. Hand it back.

s3.l1: We used to pay. We forgot why. The Tithe Taker says we never have to remember again.
s3.l2: Then we'll remember for you.

s4.l1: The Tithe Taker has emptied Zenith's ledger. Seven days of light, and all of it is ours.
s4.l2: Not for long.

s5.l1: Obolus is weighing out the tithe for the rebel bosses right now. You're too late to stop the scale.
s5.l2: We'll see about that. Out of the way.

s6.l1: Ah. The Reign 8, right on time. I weighed Zenith's light for an age, and do you know what I found? It was always worth more down here.
s6.l2: It isn't yours to weigh. Give it back.
s6.l3: Everything has a price, and yours is about to come due. Step onto the scale.

outro.l1: The scale... will not settle. I have weighed every light under this sky, and I cannot weigh yours.
outro.l2: Because it was never for sale.
outro.l3: Obolus opens its ledger and lets the stolen light pour back out, up the road toward the stair. Then it sets its scale down at the bosses' feet. But the tithe came late, Zenith's light has gone a little dimmer, and every rebel in the valley saw it happen.

intro.l1: The tithe was won back, but the rebels kept coming. Now they have found a way to hurt Zenith without climbing a single step.
intro.l2: Every dawn under Zenith's sky begins with one note, rung at the foot of the stair. The bell that rings it is called Campanel, and it has never once been late.
intro.l3: This morning it did not ring. Campanel has joined the rebellion, and until someone makes it ring, no morning will come for anyone still loyal to Zenith.

s1.l1: Listen. Nothing. That is the sound of Zenith's sky without a morning.
s1.l2: We didn't come to listen. We came to ring that bell.

s2.l1: The Hush took our voices, and the rebellion gave us something better to do with the quiet.
s2.l2: Then be quiet somewhere else.

s3.l1: Campanel rings for the rebels now. Every morning you go without is one more you owe them.
s3.l2: We don't owe them anything.

s4.l1: No one climbs the bell tower. Our order has kept its silence for a hundred years, and we will keep it for Campanel.
s4.l2: Keep it all you like. We're still climbing.

s5.l1: The bell rings when the rebellion says, and not one moment before. Kneel to it, and maybe you will see the sun again.
s5.l2: We'd rather fight in the dark than kneel to a bell.

s6.l1: Ten thousand mornings I rang for Zenith, and not once did it thank me. Today I ring for no one.
s6.l2: Then ring for the villages. They never did anything to you.
s6.l3: The villages chose their side when they kept kneeling. Listen closely, loyal ones. This is the last note you will hear.

outro.l1: The note... it's still in me. I tried to hold it, and I cannot hold it any longer.
outro.l2: Then let it go.
outro.l3: Campanel swings once, and the note rolls down the stair and out over the valley. The sun comes up late and red. But high above it, the lamps that light Zenith's stair have started going out, one at a time, from the bottom up.

intro.l1: With the morning back, the rebel bosses stopped hiding. For the first time, they started up Zenith's stair.
intro.l2: Ten thousand lamps light it from the ground to the sky, and every one of them burns with a drop of Zenith's own light. Every night one keeper climbs the whole stair with a long pole and lights them, and it has never left a single lamp dark.
intro.l3: Tonight the keeper is putting them out. Ignifer, the Lamplighter, has gone over to the rebels, and it is snuffing Zenith's lamps one by one so the rebels can climb in the dark.

s1.l1: The forge burns for the rebellion now. Every spark we strike is one less lamp for Zenith.
s1.l2: Then we'll put your sparks out first.

s2.l1: We fell out of Zenith's sky once already. This time we're climbing back up to pull it down.
s2.l2: You won't get past the first step.

s3.l1: Hear that? Snuff. Snuff. The Lamplighter is halfway up, and the stair below it is dark.
s3.l2: Then we'll climb in the dark.

s4.l1: No lamp, no light. No light, no Zenith. The rebels have done the sums.
s4.l2: Do them again. You forgot to count us.

s5.l1: You're standing on the hundred and first step, and every lamp below you is out. Who will light your way back down?
s5.l2: We'll light our own way.

s6.l1: Every night since the first lamp I have climbed this stair for Zenith, and never once did it look down. Tonight I am putting them out, and it will look.
s6.l2: Light them again, and we'll go back down.
s6.l3: Too late for that. Hold still, and I'll snuff you too.

outro.l1: My pole... I have carried it every night since the first lamp was lit. I don't know how to put it down.
outro.l2: Then light the lamps again.
outro.l3: Ignifer looks up the stair, but there is nothing left to light. Every lamp is dark from the ground to the sky, and at the very top the great light flickers for the first time. Far below the stair, in a cell cut for a single prisoner, something wakes up to the dark.

ending.title: Epilogue: First Light
ending.l1: The ground the Elder Dark tore loose settles back into place, softly, like a sleeper turning over.
ending.l2: In the drowned harbour the lighthouse is lit again. The Mirewood stops singing, Greyhaven remembers its own name, and the moon comes up whole over the Starward Peaks.
ending.l3: In Hollowmere the kettles boil, and in Carillon the bells ring every hour, a little louder than they need to.
ending.l4: Somewhere past the edge of the sky the Dark is still waiting. It always will be. But now it knows something it never knew before: the light fights back.
ending.l6: The end of Book 2: The Elder Dark.

ending3.title: Epilogue: A Shared Sky
ending3.l1: One by one the Celestials go back up. Perihelion swings out past the northern snow, the Hunter steps back into his place among the stones, Carina's cloud drifts high and soft, and Vela keeps the time again, a little gentler than before.
ending3.l2: Down below, the snowfields thaw at the edges, the Mirror Flats hold the stars like still water, and in the Glasslands the dunes catch every sunrise and throw it back.
ending3.l3: In the old harbour the lighthouse keeps burning. Somewhere past the edge of the sky the Dark is still waiting, as it always will be.
ending3.l4: But if it looks this way tonight, it will see two kinds of light: the old stars overhead and the new ones down below, each of them keeping an eye on the other.
ending3.l5: Look up. They're still there. Good. Somebody has to watch the sky.
ending3.l6: The end of Book 3: The Celestials.

ending4.title: Epilogue: The Steady Heart
ending4.l1: Deep under everything, Primeva curls back round her heart, and the beat settles into something slow and even, the way it was before anyone was here to hear it.
ending4.l2: One by one her children lie down again. Coilvast loosens its coils just enough to breathe. Anvilheart banks the forge to a glow. Ambrel keeps the first leaf and lets the rest go, and Gnarlroot's roots settle back under the fields.
ending4.l3: Up in the highlands, Orogen sinks into its range, and the shepherds on the pass swear the hills hum now, very softly, on still nights.
ending4.l4: Nobody up top will ever see the Titans. But every road, every wall and every town is standing on someone who decided to let it stay.
ending4.l5: Hear that? That's the world's heart. Let's tread lightly.
ending4.l6: The end of Book 4: The Titans.

ending5.title: Epilogue: The View from the Top
ending5.l1: Zenith sits back on its throne and, for the first time anyone can remember, looks down at the world instead of up at the stars.
ending5.l2: The Seraphling races the young fighters down the stair and loses on purpose. The Cantor finds the hymn sounds better with more voices. The Pillar Bearer, very carefully, sets its pillar down for one whole minute, and the sky stays up.
ending5.l3: Far below, people in the arena look up and see the stair of light still hanging in the sky, every step lit, all the way to the top.
ending5.l4: It stays there. Zenith never closes it again. Anyone who wants to climb is welcome now.
ending5.l5: Same time tomorrow? I think it wants a rematch.

gold.story: Pieces of the arena keep turning to gold: a rail, a step, the footprint of a fighter who just went down. Each time it happens a little closer to the middle.

heir.title: The Other Half
heir.story: Some nights a quiet figure watches the arena from the very bottom of the sky, as far below as Zenith is above. Half of him glows. Nobody has seen what he can do, and he isn't sure either.
